Andy Robertson has emphasized that bolstering Liverpool's defense is crucial for new manager Arne Slot's ambition to contend for the championship in his initial season. Although Liverpool has managed to keep their sheet clean in the first two games, their upcoming match against Manchester United at Old Trafford presents a tougher challenge. Both Ipswich and Brentford failed to score against Liverpool, allowing Slot to commence his tenure with solid defensive performances. In the previous season, Liverpool allowed 41 goals across 38 games, finishing third, which was more compared to champions Manchester City who conceded seven fewer, and Arsenal, who conceded 12 fewer. However, Robertson noted that the initial matches of the new season show positive signs, including two consecutive games without conceding a goal.

Handle the upcoming games with resilience, especially the imminent match against Manchester United, is a sentiment strongly expressed by Robertson. He hopes that Liverpool will continue their robust defensive setup and minimize Manchester United’s opportunities to score. The team also looks forward to maintaining strong defensive performances against other teams following the international break. Reflecting on the last season, Robertson acknowledged that Liverpool were at a defensive disadvantage compared to Arsenal and Manchester City, even while they were still in contention for the title. He pointed out that allowing more chances eventually led to losses that could be avoided, emphasizing the need for tighter defense this season to avoid similar setbacks.

Robertson’s current outlook is one of cautious optimism. He and his teammates are aware of the challenges ahead but are encouraged by their promising start under Slot’s leadership. The strategic focus on defense, according to Robertson, will be crucial in their quest for the Premier League title, aiming to rectify the previous season’s shortcomings. As they gear up for more demanding matches, the team’s ability to sustain their defensive form will be tested, but the early instances of success give them confidence moving forward.
